extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs), environmental compliance officers, and permitting/compliance staff responsible for 40 CFR part 60 subpart TTTT/TTTTa compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and detailed procedures for demonstrating and reporting compliance with CO2 emission standards for affected steam generating units, IGCCs, and stationary combustion turbines under 40 CFR part 60 subparts TTTT and TTTTa. Covers applicability, monitoring, calculations, reporting, recordkeeping, definitions, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total gross or net energy output (output-based standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are subject to an output-based standard, you must calculate the total gross or net energy output for the affected EGU's compliance period by summing the hourly gross or net energy output values for the affected EGU that you determined under paragraph (a)(5) of this section for all of the valid operating hours in the applicable compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per §60.5520 and referenced paragraph (a)(5); use only 'valid operating hours' as defined elsewhere in the subpart. Sum hourly values for the applicable compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total heat input by fuel (heat input-based standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are subject to a heat input-based standard, you must calculate the total heat input for each fuel fired during the compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The calculation of total heat input for each individual fuel must include all valid operating hours and must be consistent with any fuel-specific procedures specified within your selected monitoring option under §60.5535(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 mass emissions rate calculation (output- and input-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: For output-based standards: calculate CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/MWh) by dividing the total CO2 mass emissions value by the total gross or net energy output. For heat input-based standards: calculate CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu) by dividing the total CO2 mass emissions value by the total heat input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round off the result to two significant figures if the calculated value is less than 1,000; round the result to three significant figures if the calculated value is greater than 1,000. (Printed page note: Round off the result to two significant figures.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of compliance on 12-operating-month basis
rubrics_metrics.description: To demonstrate compliance for the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month compliance period, the CO2 mass emissions rate for your affected EGU must be determined according to the specified procedures and must be less than or equal to the applicable CO2 emissions standard in table 1 or 2 to this subpart, or the emissions standard calculated in accordance with §60.5525(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is determined on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis; determine compliance monthly by calculating the average at the end of each 12-operating-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report percentage of valid operating hours
rubrics_metrics.description: You must report the percentage of valid operating hours in each 12-operating-month compliance period (i.e., the total number of valid operating hours in that period divided by the total number of operating hours in that period, multiplied by 100 percent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required as part of the reports under §60.5555(a)(2)(iv). 'Valid operating hours' is defined in §60.5540(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report applicable CO2 emissions standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §60.5520, you must report the CO2 emissions standard (as identified in table 1 or 2 to this subpart) with which your affected EGU must comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required in periodic reporting per §60.5555.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting when CO2 capture used to meet standard
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the applicable emissions standard, you must report in accordance with the requirements of 40 CFR part 98, subpart PP, and either report in accordance with 40 CFR part 98, subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; transfer the captured CO2 to an EGU or facility that reports under subpart RR or VV if injection occurs off-site; or transfer to a facility that has received an innovative technology waiver from EPA pursuant to paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies reporting pathways depending on on-site injection, off-site injection, or if an innovative technology waiver has been issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver criteria for innovative CO2 storage technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request a waiver that captured CO2 need not be transferred to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV by demonstrating that the technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and will not cause or contribute to an unreasonable risk to public health, welfare, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator will consider operating history, whether the technology increases other emissions, and permanence of CO2 storage; Administrator may test systems or require tests, may grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting, may withdraw approval upon evidence of releases, and will provide public notice of applications and proposed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of electric sales for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: For stationary combustion turbines, you must keep records of electric sales to determine the applicable subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to demonstrate whether a turbine is subject to gross/net/heat input-based standards per §60.5520(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records to demonstrate operation during a system emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records to demonstrate that your affected facility operated during a system emergency, including documentation that the system emergency was in effect (with duration), documentation that the emergency included the affected source/region, and documentation that the facility was instructed to increase output or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch by a Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, or ISO/RTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records are listed in §60.5560(i)(1)-(3) and are necessary to exclude those hours from applicability/compliance in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Annual capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual capacity factor means the ratio between the actual heat input to an EGU during a calendar year and the potential heat input to the EGU had it been operated for 8,760 hours during a calendar year at the base load rating. Actual and potential heat input derived from non-combustion sources are not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how to calculate annual capacity factor for applicability and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Base load rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Base load rating means the maximum amount of heat input (fuel) that an EGU can combust on a steady state basis plus the maximum amount of heat input derived from non-combustion source, as determined by the physical design and characteristics of the EGU at ISO conditions. For a stationary combustion turbine, base load rating includes the heat input from duct burners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for applicability thresholds and emission standard categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Coal
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal means all solid fuels classified as anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, or lignite by ASTM D388-99R04, coal refuse, and petroleum coke. Synthetic fuels derived from coal for useful heat are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites incorporated ASTM standard; lists included synthetic fuel types for purposes of the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined cycle unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined cycle unit means a stationary combustion turbine from which the heat from the turbine exhaust gases is recovered by an HRSG to generate additional electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies unit types for applicability and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined heat and power (CHP) unit
rubrics_metrics.description: CHP unit (cogeneration) means an electric generating unit that simultaneously produces both electric (or mechanical) and useful thermal output from the same primary energy source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in applicability and net-electric sales definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Design efficiency and approved methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Design efficiency means the rated overall net efficiency on a lower heating value basis at the base load rating, at ISO conditions, and at the maximum useful thermal output. Design efficiency shall be determined using one of the following methods: ASME PTC 22-2014, ASME PTC 46-1996, ISO 2314:2009(E), or an alternative approved by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable test standards or Administrator-approved alternatives for determining design efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Distillate oil specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Distillate oil means fuel oils that comply with specifications in ASTM D396-98, diesel fuel oil numbers 1 and 2 per ASTM D975-08a, kerosene per ASTM D3699-08, biodiesel per ASTM D6751-11b, or biodiesel blends per ASTM D7467-10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References ASTM standards for fuel classification relevant to monitoring and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: ISO conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: ISO conditions means 288 Kelvin (15 °C, 59 °F), 60 percent relative humidity and 101.3 kilopascals pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for base load rating and design efficiency determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net-electric sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Net-electric sales means (1) gross electric sales to the utility power distribution system minus purchased power; or (2) for CHP facilities meeting certain thresholds, gross electric sales to the utility minus purchased power of the thermal host facility or facilities. Electricity supplied to other facilities that produce electricity to offset auxiliary loads are included. Electric sales during a system emergency are not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for CHP facilities and exclusion of emergency hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: System emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: System emergency means periods when the Reliability Coordinator has declared an Energy Emergency Alert level 2 or 3 as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2 or its successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to exclude certain operations from applicability/compliance when proper documentation is kept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1: CO2 emission standards for affected steam generating units and IGCC
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists CO2 emission standards for newly constructed, reconstructed (<=2,100 GJ/h and >2,100 GJ/h), and modified steam generating units/IGCCs (unit-specific emission limit determined by unit's best historical annual CO2 emission rate but no lower than specified floors). Note: numerical values of 1,000 or greater have min 3 significant figures; <1,000 have min 2 significant figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Newly constructed: 640 kg CO2/MWh gross (1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross). Reconstructed small: 910 kg CO2/MWh gross (2,000 lb). Reconstructed large: 820 kg CO2/MWh gross (1,800 lb). Modified units: unit-specific limit not lower than 820 or 910 kg/MWh depending on base load rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2: CO2 emission standards for affected stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists CO2 emission standards for newly constructed or reconstructed stationary combustion turbines with different operating/net-electric sales characteristics and fuel combusted, including both gross and net energy output-based limits and heat input-based limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Certain newly constructed/reconstructed turbines combusting >90% natural gas and meeting net-electric sales thresholds: 450 kg CO2/MWh gross or 470 kg CO2/MWh net; alternative heat-input standard: 50 kg CO2/GJ (120 lb/MMBtu). Other categories and ranges (50 to 69 kg CO2/GJ) are determined per §60.5525 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability criteria for subpart TTTTa (construction/reconstruction dates and thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart applies to steam generating units/IGCCs that commence modification after May 23, 2023 and stationary combustion turbines that commence construction or reconstruction after May 23, 2023, with base load rating >260 GJ/h and serving generator(s) capable of selling >25 MW to a utility distribution system, except as provided in exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §60.5508a and §60.5509a for full applicability and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from subpart TTTTa
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources are not subject to subpart if they meet any of listed conditions, such as: (1) annual net-electric sales never exceeded one-third of potential or 219,000 MWh and enforceable permit limiting sales; (2) capable of deriving ≥50% heat input from non-fossil and subject to permit limiting annual fossil fuel capacity factor ≤10%; (3) CHP unit with enforceable sales limit; (4) serves generator with effective generation capacity ≤25 MW when pro-rated; (5) municipal waste combustor subject to subpart Eb; (6) CISWI unit subject to subpart CCCC; (7) modification resulting in hourly CO2 increase ≤10%; (8) derives >50% heat input from industrial process that produces no electrical/mechanical/useful thermal output used outside the EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific numeric thresholds and permit condition requirements determine exemptions; modified units excluded under (7) remain existing units under section 111 for CO2 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG regulated pollutant(s) identification and PSD/Title V mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: The pollutants regulated are greenhouse gases, and the greenhouse gas standard is a limitation on CO2 emissions. For PSD and Title V thresholds, the 'pollutant subject to the standard promulgated under section 111' shall be considered the pollutant otherwise subject to regulation under the Act as defined in various 40 CFR provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides cross-references for permitting thresholds and regulatory interpretation in 40 CFR parts 51, 52, 70, and 71.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross vs net energy output standard selection and petition process
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified, owners/operators must comply with the applicable gross or net energy output standard and have monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting methodologies based on the applicable gross or net energy output standard. A stationary combustion turbine owner/operator may petition the Administrator to comply with the alternate net energy output standard; if granted, the operating permit and monitoring must be based on net output. Owners/operators can petition to switch back to gross standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies permit and monitoring alignment with chosen basis and requires written petition to Administrator for net-output election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform fuels exemption for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines permitted to burn only fuels with a consistent chemical composition ('uniform fuels') that result in a consistent emission rate of 69 kg/GJ (160 lb/MMBtu) or less are not subject to any monitoring or reporting requirements under this subpart other than maintaining purchase records for permitted fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform fuels include hydrogen, natural gas, methane, butane, butylene, ethane, ethylene, propane, naphtha, propylene, jet fuel, kerosene, No. 1 fuel oil, No. 2 fuel oil, and biodiesel. This exemption applies only to fuels with consistent composition and emission rate ≤69 kg/GJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring obligations for turbines burning non-uniform or higher-emitting fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of turbines permitted to burn non-uniform fuels or fuels with emission rate >69 kg/GJ must follow monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements necessary to complete heat input-based calculations under the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those sources must follow the monitoring procedures in §60.5535a and related provisions to quantify heat input and CO2 emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement: comply at all times; determination monthly
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be in compliance with the emission standards at all times. However, you must determine compliance only at the end of the applicable operating month by calculating the average CO2 emissions rate for the affected EGU at the end of the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is continuous, but measurement/assessment uses monthly determination tied to 12-operating-month rolling average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input-based emissions standard equation and site-specific rate elections
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an input-based standard, owners/operators must determine total heat input from natural gas and all other fuels and use the specified equation (Equation 1) to determine the applicable emissions standard during the compliance period. Owners/operators of certain base or intermediate load turbines may elect to determine a site-specific emissions rate using Equation 2 (base load) or Equation 3 (intermediate load) with defined parameters (BLER, BLR, HIER, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equations include parameters like allowable emission rates (50 kg/GJ for natural gas; 69 kg/GJ for other fuels), base load emissions rates (BLER) with numeric example values, and caps such as HIER_A not to exceed 69 kg/GJ (160 lb/MMBtu).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation and maintenance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times you must operate and maintain each affected EGU, including associated equipment and monitors, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator will determine if consistent O&M practices are used based on fuel use records, monitoring results, review of procedures and records, reports, and inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance determination timing and first operating month rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the end of the initial compliance period (no more than 30 days after the first 12-operating-month compliance period), you must make an initial compliance determination. The first operating month included in the initial compliance period depends on whether unit commences commercial operation or is modified/reconstructed and on whether subject to Acid Rain Program/other reporting triggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §60.5525a(c)(1)-(2) for the specific triggers (e.g., emissions reporting required to begin under §60.5555a(c)(3)(i)-(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of emissions/output during system emergencies (with documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions of CO2 emitted and the output generated when an affected facility operated during a system emergency are excluded for both applicability and compliance with relevant standards if you can sufficiently provide the documentation listed in §60.5560a(i). The relevant standard depends on subcategory (e.g., intermediate and base load turbines operating during a system emergency comply with the low load combustion turbine standard in table 1; modified steam generating units must not discharge gases containing CO2 in excess of 230 lb CO2/MMBtu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires recordkeeping per §60.5560a(i) to qualify for exclusion; specifies alternative standards applicable during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan and ECMPS submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For all affected sources (except turbines qualifying under uniform fuel exemption), you must prepare a monitoring plan to quantify hourly CO2 mass emission rate in accordance with 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h). The electronic portion must be submitted using the ECMPS Client Tool and must be in place prior to reporting emissions data or monitoring system certification results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plan must be updated as necessary and submitted by the Designated Representative (DR), Alternate DR, or delegated agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS installation and alternative O2-based method
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affected EGU that combusts coal you must, and for all other affected EGUs you may, install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a CO2 continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) to directly measure hourly average CO2 concentrations and a flow monitoring system. As an alternative to direct CO2 concentration measurement (provided EGU does not use carbon separation), you may use data from a certified O2 monitor to calculate hourly average CO2 concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If measuring CO2 on a dry basis, you must also install a continuous moisture monitoring system or use an appropriate default moisture value from 40 CFR 75.11(b) or petition for a site-specific default via 40 CFR 75.66.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and QA/QC for continuous monitoring systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For each continuous monitoring system used to determine CO2 mass emissions, you must meet the applicable certification and quality assurance procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B to 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to CO2 concentration, flow, and moisture monitoring systems used for emissions calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates (no bias adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use only unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates to determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions rate from the affected EGU; you must not apply the bias adjustment factors described in Section 7.6.5 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 to the exhaust gas flow rate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow data used in calculations must be raw/unadjusted per this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow monitor reference method selection and pitot tube calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: You must select an appropriate reference method to setup (characterize) the flow monitor and to perform the on-going RATAs, in accordance with 40 CFR part 75. If you use a Type-S pitot tube or a pitot tube assembly for the flow RATAs, you must calibrate the pitot tube or pitot tube assembly; you may not use the 0.84 default Type-S pitot tube coefficient specified in Method 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures accurate flow monitor characterization and RATA practices; prohibits use of default uncalibrated coefficient for Type-S pitot assemblies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly CO2 mass emissions calculation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the hourly CO2 mass emissions (kg) by: (i) obtaining the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) using Equation F-11 in appendix F to 40 CFR part 75 (wet basis) or procedure in section 4.2 of appendix F (dry basis); (ii) multiplying each hourly CO2 mass emission rate by the EGU/stack operating time to convert to tons of CO2; (iii) multiplying by 907.2 to convert tons to kg and rounding to the nearest kg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform calculations only for 'valid operating hours' per §60.5540(a)(1). The hourly tons/h values and operating times are required to be recorded under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and reported electronically under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6); use these data for the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative hourly CO2 calculation for liquid/gaseous fuel-only EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU exclusively combusts liquid fuel and/or gaseous fuel, as an alternative to complying with paragraph (b) (i.e., CEMS-based approach), you may determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions according to paragraphs (c)(1) through (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chunk references this alternative method but full procedural detail is in subsequent paragraphs; signals that alternatives exist for certain fuel types.
